evals.prompt: I need clean markdown from https://example.com/blog-post — can you scrape it and save the article content, ignoring the nav and footer?
evals.expected_output: A markdown file containing the article body from the page with navigation and footer boilerplate removed.
assertions: The output is a .md file with the article's headings and paragraphs
The output excludes the site's navigation and footer content
The script uses AsyncWebCrawler with a PruningContentFilter or equivalent

evals.prompt: Extract all products from https://example.com/shop into a JSON array with name, price, and product URL. There are many product cards on the page.
evals.expected_output: A JSON array where each item has name, price, and url fields for every product card on the page.
assertions: Each item contains the fields name, price, and url
The extraction uses a JsonCssExtractionStrategy schema (no LLM)

evals.prompt: The page https://example.com/dynamic loads its list via a 'Load More' button. Get me all 50 items without triggering rate limits.
evals.expected_output: All 50 items from the dynamic list, obtained by clicking the Load More button and waiting for content, with polite pacing.
assertions: The script uses js_code and/or wait_for to click and await dynamic content
All 50 items are present in the result
The script includes a delay or cache_mode setting to avoid hammering the site

evals.prompt:
Convert this HTML snippet to markdown:

Title

Body text
evals.expected_output: A short markdown conversion showing # Title and Body text. (Negative control: agent can do this without the skill.)
assertions: The output is plain markdown with the heading and body text
No AsyncWebCrawler, BrowserConfig, or extraction strategy is introduced for this trivial conversion
